b: While one sustains life and the other will sicken or kill you, explaining saltwater's difference in taste and properties from freshwater wouldn't have been obvious to premodern people since the ions that make ocean water salty are invisible to the naked eye. If a population lived near large halite deposits and the ocean, perhaps they would make a connection between dissolved minerals in freshwater and the taste of saltwater.

What were some beliefs about the difference in what we know understand as salinity? I imagine there was great diversity of mythological beliefs and reasoned explanations across space and time, and I'd appreciate some examples. Thanks!
